summary: This document is a TRL 2 project description for bufotenine prodrugs designed as CNS-penetrant 5-HT2A agonists for psychiatric indications. The project is entirely computational/analytical at this stage — no synthesis or biological experiments have been conducted. It outlines a staged in silico campaign (WPs 1–6) to identify and triage prodrug candidates, with a defined path to TRL 3 wet-lab proof-of-concept.

content_blocks.title: Concept Statement and Technology Overview
content_blocks.content: Bufotenine (5-HO-DMT) is a potent 5-HT2A agonist in vitro but has poor CNS penetration due to its free 5-hydroxyl group, which increases polarity and ionization at physiological pH. The proposed concept is to transiently mask the 5-OH group to create a CNS-penetrant prodrug, analogous to the psilocybin (4-PO-DMT → psilocin) precedent. The intended application is a controlled-duration, orally or intranasally dosed serotonergic agent for psychiatric indications. TRL is explicitly stated as 2 (technology concept and/or application formulated). Work type is analytical and computational only — no synthesis, no biological material, no in vivo work.

content_blocks.title: Problem Statement: Limitations of Existing Toad-Derived Psychedelics
content_blocks.content:
Two-column table comparing bufotenine and 5-MeO-DMT:
- Bufotenine (5-HO-DMT): High polarity and ionization at pH 7.4; poor and route-dependent CNS exposure; prominent peripheral cardiovascular effects at doses needed for central activity.
- 5-MeO-DMT: Good BBB penetration but very rapid onset and ~10–20 min duration; difficult to titrate; limited therapeutic window for psychological support.
The prodrug concept targets the gap between them.

content_blocks.title: Underlying Scientific Rationale
content_blocks.content:
Four pillars of rationale are provided:
1. Precedent: Psilocybin is a naturally occurring phosphate ester prodrug of psilocin; dephosphorylation by alkaline phosphatase during first pass yields the active phenol, establishing that phenolic masking on a DMT scaffold is metabolically tractable and clinically viable.
2. Physicochemistry: Masking the 5-OH removes a hydrogen-bond donor, lowers TPSA, and raises logD at pH 7.4 — the three parameters most strongly driving passive CNS penetration in the tryptamine series.
3. Kinetic control: Ester, carbamate, and phosphate promoieties hydrolyse at different rates, making the rate of unmasking a design variable for tuning duration and onset.
4. Metabolic protection: Bufotenine is a MAO substrate; a promoiety shielding the molecule during first pass may reduce presystemic MAO clearance.

content_blocks.title: Central Hypothesis
content_blocks.content: "Bufotenine analogs bearing hydrolysable 5-position promoieties will show predicted CNS penetration comparable to 5-MeO-DMT while retaining 5-HT2A binding of the released parent, with a 5-HT2A/5-HT2B selectivity margin at least as favourable as bufotenine itself." This is a computational hypothesis only — no experimental data are presented to support or refute it at this stage.

content_blocks.title: WP1 — Physicochemical Baseline and Model Validation
content_blocks.content: Compute pKa (tertiary amine, indole NH, 5-OH), logP, logD₇.₄, TPSA, HBD/HBA counts, and CNS multiparameter optimisation (MPO) score for a reference panel: bufotenine, 5-MeO-DMT, DMT, psilocin, psilocybin, serotonin. Purpose: the panel has a known experimental rank order of CNS penetration; if predictors do not reproduce that rank order, they are not fit for purpose. Go/no-go gate: predicted BBB ranking must place 5-MeO-DMT and DMT above bufotenine and serotonin. Status: planned (no results reported).

content_blocks.title: WP2 — Virtual Analog Library Enumeration
content_blocks.content: Enumerate 150–300 bufotenine derivatives across promoiety classes: simple alkyl and aryl esters, carbonate and carbamate esters, phosphate and phosphoramidate esters, and amino-acid conjugates (targeting peptide transporter uptake). Output: enumerated, physicochemically annotated library with predicted hydrolytic half-lives estimated from published ester-hydrolysis QSAR. Status: planned.

content_blocks.title: WP3 — Receptor Docking and Selectivity Triage
content_blocks.content: Dock released parent compound and large promoieties against active-state 5-HT2A, 5-HT2B (counter-target for valvular heart disease liability, as seen with fenfluramine and pergolide), and 5-HT1A. PDB structures to be confirmed at project start. Go/no-go gate: retain only series with predicted 5-HT2A preference over 5-HT2B. Status: planned.

content_blocks.title: WP4 — Molecular Dynamics and Binding Free Energy
content_blocks.content: For top 10–20 candidates, run MD simulations of ligand–receptor complexes and estimate relative binding free energies by MM-GBSA or FEP. Assess stability of toggle-switch and conserved binding-pocket contacts characteristic of agonist engagement. Explicit limitation stated: docking and free-energy methods rank affinity, not efficacy or signalling bias; computational prediction of Gq vs. β-arrestin bias is not currently reliable and no bias claims will be made from this WP. Status: planned.

content_blocks.title: WP5 — ADMET and Liability Profiling
content_blocks.content: Predict hERG inhibition, CYP inhibition and induction, MAO-A/B substrate likelihood, hepatotoxicity flags, and aqueous solubility. Cross-check hits against structural alerts. Status: planned.

content_blocks.title: WP6 — Prior Art and Freedom-to-Operate Scan
content_blocks.content: Systematic literature and patent search on 5-position tryptamine prodrugs. The psilocybin analog space is heavily patented and the psychedelic IP landscape moves quickly; this scan must be run fresh and cannot be inherited from a prior review. Status: planned.

content_blocks.title: TRL 2 Success Criteria
content_blocks.content: The stage is complete when the project can present: (1) A validated physicochemical prediction workflow (WP1 gate passed); (2) At least 5 designed candidates with predicted CNS penetration in the 5-MeO-DMT range; (3) A predicted 5-HT2A/5-HT2B selectivity rationale for the retained series; (4) A documented FTO position; (5) A written, costed wet-lab protocol ready to execute — the actual handover artifact to TRL 3.

content_blocks.title: Deliverables
content_blocks.content: Planned deliverables at TRL 2 completion: (1) Computational methods report with validation data; (2) Annotated virtual library (structures, descriptors, predicted properties); (3) Docking and MD results package with explicit confidence statements; (4) Prior art / FTO memorandum; (5) TRL 3 experimental protocol covering: radioligand binding, functional cAMP/IP1 assay, PAMPA-BBB or MDCK-MDR1 permeability, and hydrolysis stability in plasma and simulated intestinal fluid.

content_blocks.title: Risk Register
content_blocks.content:
Five risks identified with severity and mitigation:
1. In silico BBB predictors have modest accuracy for zwitterionic/ionizable species (this chemotype) — Severity: High — Mitigation: WP1 validation gate; treat all predictions as hypothesis-generating only.
2. Promoiety hydrolysis may be too fast (no benefit) or too slow (no active drug released) — Severity: High — Mitigation: Deliberate spread of promoiety classes across a hydrolysis-rate range.
3. Peripheral cardiovascular effects may be intrinsic to bufotenine, not a consequence of poor penetration — Severity: Medium — Mitigation: Explicit falsification test designed into TRL 3 protocol.
4. 5-HT2B liability may not be separable within this scaffold — Severity: Medium — Mitigation: Early counter-screen; kill criterion defined before work begins.
5. Crowded IP landscape — Severity: Medium — Mitigation: WP6 executed early, not at the end.
Core assumption requiring wet-lab falsification: bufotenine's weak psychoactivity is predominantly a pharmacokinetic problem rather than a pharmacodynamic one.

content_blocks.title: Regulatory and Compliance Notes
content_blocks.content: Bufotenine and 5-MeO-DMT are Schedule I in the United States and controlled in most jurisdictions. Computational work on structures is not itself restricted, but downstream synthesis, possession, or handling requires appropriate controlled-substance licensing and institutional approvals before TRL 3 begins. Novel analogs may fall under analog-substance provisions in some jurisdictions — legal review required before physical work. If any project stage contemplates animal-derived material, Nagoya Protocol access-and-benefit-sharing obligations and CITES status of source species apply.

content_blocks.title: Path to TRL 3
content_blocks.content: TRL 3 is reached on first experimental proof of concept: synthesis of 3–5 prioritised candidates under licence, followed by demonstration that (a) the promoiety hydrolyses to release bufotenine at a usable rate in plasma, and (b) the prodrug shows measurably improved permeability over bufotenine in a cell-based BBB model. No timeline or date is specified for TRL 3 initiation.

key_findings: Project is explicitly at TRL 2 — technology concept formulated; all work to date is analytical/computational only with no synthesis, biological material, or in vivo experiments.

Core concept: masking the 5-OH group of bufotenine (5-HO-DMT) with hydrolysable promoieties (esters, carbamates, phosphates, amino-acid conjugates) to improve CNS penetration, analogous to the psilocybin/psilocin precedent.
Central hypothesis is unvalidated: bufotenine prodrugs will show predicted CNS penetration comparable to 5-MeO-DMT while retaining 5-HT2A binding and a favourable 5-HT2A/5-HT2B selectivity margin.
No experimental data are presented; all six work packages (WP1–WP6) are planned but not yet executed.
Key go/no-go gate in WP1: predicted BBB ranking must place 5-MeO-DMT and DMT above bufotenine and serotonin using a reference panel of six tryptamines.
Virtual library of 150–300 bufotenine derivatives planned across multiple promoiety classes (WP2).
5-HT2B counter-screening is a defined kill criterion — 5-HT2B agonism is linked to valvular heart disease (fenfluramine/pergolide precedent).
Explicit limitation acknowledged: computational methods rank affinity, not efficacy or signalling bias; no Gq vs. β-arrestin bias claims will be made.
Core assumption requiring wet-lab falsification: bufotenine's weak psychoactivity is predominantly a pharmacokinetic (not pharmacodynamic) problem.
Regulatory barrier: bufotenine and 5-MeO-DMT are Schedule I; controlled-substance licensing required before any TRL 3 synthesis or handling.
IP landscape risk: psilocybin analog space is heavily patented; FTO scan (WP6) must be executed early.

TRL 3 handover artifact is a written, costed wet-lab protocol covering radioligand binding, cAMP/IP1 functional assay, PAMPA-BBB or MDCK-MDR1 permeability, and hydrolysis stability in plasma and simulated intestinal fluid.
No funding, team, or partnership information is disclosed in this document.
